summary: RuleResult (survivors/best_match/count/explain/at_least accessors, plus select() to re-apply a hit policy post-hoc) and ExplainResult (every rule scored, unfiltered, for explain()). select() now validates the policy and priority field, gates re-selection on non-truncated selection info, and its output is re-sorted by __rank; best_match sorts by __rank before taking the top row instead of trusting caller row order.
lifecycle_notes: ExplainResult exposes unfiltered scoring without ranked-selection methods; it is not a RuleResult subclass.
RuleResult.select(policy) requires explicit selection metadata and the complete candidate basis; manually wrapping a dataframe does not establish that provenance.

select() now accepts HitPolicy | str and normalizes/validates it via hit_policy.normalize_policy() (raises ValueError on an unknown policy string instead of failing later); it also validates an explicit priority_field via validate_priority_field() and requires the '__rank' column in addition to '__specificity'/'__rule_index'.

select() runs check_policy_config()/check_priority() (new hit_policy.py gates) before re-sorting/re-ranking, then sets the returned RuleResult's selection_info.truncated via selection_is_truncated(policy) instead of copying the original info unchanged — previously a second select() after FIRST/PRIORITY/ANY could silently re-select from an already-truncated single-row set; now it correctly raises the 'possibly truncated' ValueError.

select()'s returned dataframe is now explicitly re-sorted by '__rank' before collect(), and best_match now does relation(...).sort('__rank').head(1) instead of a bare head(1) — both accessors no longer assume the incoming frame is pre-sorted by the caller.
risks: best_match requires a __rank column and follows the minimum retained rank, not necessarily the most specific rule under every policy.

evidence.detail: ExplainResult is a separate class without __rank, best_match or select; its frame includes both surviving and rejected rules.

select(): normalize_policy(policy), validate_priority_field(priority_field), check_policy_config(rel.columns, selected_policy, selected_info), check_priority(rel, selected_policy, selected_info), and selection_info=replace(selected_info, truncated=selection_is_truncated(selected_policy)) on return
